_: The five findings of the red (Screening) hero, in the EXACT keys lot S1 declared (message of the night of 5 to 6). Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-screening/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; S1 refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches that seal, and this file names each figure's cell in `source` beside it: {table, palier, seuil, mesure} reads releve[table].tables[palier][seuil][mesure] ({succes, n, taux, bas, haut}); {table, compte} reads releve[table][compte]. `source` is provenance for reviewers and future guards; builders may ignore it. Intervals in legends are Wilson 95% from the same cells, en dash, never an em dash. The rule behind finding 03 is the tool's own default (optimise: Wilson lower bound of recall >= 0.90, then the fewest false alerts), the same rule the live instrument applies: one rule on the whole site, chosen, not measured, and said on the fiche. `annotations` are fractions of the rendered tower box (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text), placed by the chef on the rendered states.

findings.titre: Exact never alarms. It also never finds.
findings.phrase: Exact match after normalisation raises no false alert on our written pairs, and that safety is the trap: it misses four true hits in five that your reviewers already confirmed.
findings.leg_a: recall on the 60 written match pairs, interval [13–34]: any threshold, exact is flat
findings.leg_b: false alerts on the 60 written non-match pairs, interval [0–6]
annotations: the strict sieve, at the top: a few hits, no noise
the loosest sieve, at the bottom: every hit is still there

findings.titre: Loose matching finds everyone. And everyone else.
findings.phrase: Drop the threshold and nothing escapes: every true hit is caught. So is most of everything unrelated, and every false alert is analyst time you pay for.
findings.leg_a: recall at the loosest threshold of the sweep, interval [94–100], 60 match pairs
findings.leg_b: false alerts at the same threshold, interval [74–92], 60 non-match pairs
annotations: the loose sieve: nothing escapes, nothing is filtered
the grey ones are false alerts, nearly one per hit

findings.titre: The frontier lives in the middle.
findings.phrase: Hold the lower bound of measured recall at 90 percent, the tool's own default rule, and the sweep of every tier and threshold, the embedding included, settles on one cell. Even there, three alerts in four are false.
findings.leg_a: recall of the retained cell, jaro‑winkler at 0.56, interval [91–100]
findings.leg_b: false alerts at that same cell, interval [65–86]: the price of the floor
annotations: the ruby frame: the sieve the frontier retains
what it still lets through lies at the foot

findings.titre: Synthetic is declared. And never merged.
findings.phrase: The same cell, two provenances. On fabricated variants the false-alert rate reads far friendlier than on written pairs: blended, the synthetic half would flatter the tool. It is measured apart, labelled synthetic, and stays apart.
findings.leg_a: false alerts at the frontier cell, measured on the 60 written pairs, interval [65–86]
findings.leg_b: the same cell on 360 fabricated variants, interval [14–21]: kept apart precisely because it flatters

findings.phrase: Every pair behind these findings is ours: written and declared, or fabricated and labelled. One command replays the whole sweep on your own alert history, on your machine. Nothing leaves it.
findings.leg_a: written pairs behind the measured half, declared nature by nature
findings.leg_b: fabricated variants behind the synthetic half, labelled and kept apart
annotations: our pairs end where your export begins
measure:yours, next to your file: uncoloured until measured
